paper_title: Bootstrapping SU(3) lattice Yang-Mills theory (Guo, 2025, JHEP)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
Fix $N\in\{2,3\}$, $d\in\{2,3,4\}$, $\lambda>0$, and a finite truncation $T$ retaining the plaquette coordinate $x_P$. Let $F_{N,d,T,\lambda}$ be the real feasible set obtained by imposing exactly the retained normalization, positivity constraints, Schwinger--Dyson equalities, and the applicable $SU(2)$ or $SU(3)$ trace reductions. If the exact Yang--Mills retained moment assignment belongs to this set, then
\[
L_{N,d,T}(\lambda):=\inf_{X\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}}x_P(X),\qquad
U_{N,d,T}(\lambda):=\sup_{X\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}}x_P(X)
\]
certify the exact plaquette value $p_{N,d}(\lambda)=\langle w(P)\rangle$:
\[
L_{N,d,T}(\lambda)\leq p_{N,d}(\lambda)\leq U_{N,d,T}(\lambda).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}\text{ is the restriction of the exact Yang--Mills moment functional to the coordinates retained by }T.\\[0.4em]
\text{(P2)} & x_P(X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda})=p_{N,d}(\lambda).\\[0.4em]
\text{(P3)} & \text{Hermitian positivity gives }A^H_{ab}=\langle\operatorname{tr}(P_a^\dagger P_b)\rangle\succeq0\text{ for retained common-endpoint paths.}\\[0.4em]
\text{(P4)} & \text{Ordinary reflection positivity gives }A^R_{ab}=\langle\operatorname{tr}(\Theta[P_a]P_b)\rangle\succeq0\text{ for retained mirror path sets.}\\[0.4em]
\text{(P5)} & \text{Every retained link variation supplies an exact Schwinger--Dyson equality for }X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}.\\[0.4em]
\text{(P6)} & \text{The }SU(2)\text{ and }SU(3)\text{ trace reductions are exact identities whenever their variables are retained.}\\[0.4em]
\text{(P7)} & X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}\text{ follows from (P3)--(P6).}
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Because $X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}$,
\begin{align}
L_{N,d,T}(\lambda)
&=\inf_{X\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}}x_P(X)\\
&\leq x_P(X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}) && \text{infimum over a set containing }X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}\\
&=p_{N,d}(\lambda) && \text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
Similarly,
\begin{align}
U_{N,d,T}(\lambda)
&=\sup_{X\in F_{N,d,T,\lambda}}x_P(X)\\
&\geq x_P(X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}) && \text{supremum over a set containing }X^\ast_{N,d,T,\lambda}\\
&=p_{N,d}(\lambda) && \text{by (P2)}.
\end{align}
Combining the two inequalities gives the claimed certificate.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{L_{N,d,T}(\lambda)\leq p_{N,d}(\lambda)\leq U_{N,d,T}(\lambda)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\section*{Claim}
In $d=2$, twist-reflection positivity is an exact validity-preserving augmentation of the plaquette bootstrap, but the same exact conclusion must not be exported to $d\geq3$ from the two-dimensional proof alone. For
\[
R_t(x,y)=(-x,-y),
\qquad \Theta_t[P]=R_t[P]^\dagger,
\qquad
A^t_{ab}=\left\langle\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Theta_t[P_a]P_b\bigr)\right\rangle,
\]
the exact two-dimensional moment assignment satisfies $A^t\succeq0$. Therefore, adding retained constraints $A^t\succeq0$ in $d=2$ gives the nested bounds of the augmentation theorem.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{(P1)} & P_1,\ldots,P_M\text{ are retained paths in the positive half-plane with endpoints at the origin.}\\[0.4em]
\text{(P2)} & \text{In }d=2\text{ one may gauge-fix the separating line so that }U_{0+}=U_{0-}=1.\\[0.4em]
\text{(P3)} & F:=\sum_{a=1}^M c_aP_a\text{ with }c_a\in\mathbb{R}.\\[0.4em]
\text{(P4)} & \displaystyle \int DU\,e^{-S}\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Theta_t[F]F\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(Q^\dagger Q)\text{ for the corresponding half-plane integral }Q.\\[0.6em]
\text{(P5)} & \operatorname{tr}(Q^\dagger Q)\geq0.\\[0.4em]
\text{(P6)} & \text{For }d\geq3\text{ the twist-reflection factorization is not an exact retained premise.}
\end{array}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Normalize (P4) by the positive partition function $Z$ and use (P5):
\begin{align}
\left\langle\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Theta_t[F]F\bigr)\right\rangle\geq0.
\end{align}
By real linearity of $F$ and antilinearity of $\Theta_t$ with real coefficients,
\begin{align}
\Theta_t[F]F
&=\left(\sum_{a=1}^M c_a\Theta_t[P_a]\right)\left(\sum_{b=1}^M c_bP_b\right)\\
&=\sum_{a,b=1}^M c_ac_b\Theta_t[P_a]P_b.
\end{align}
Taking trace and expectation gives
\begin{align}
\left\langle\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Theta_t[F]F\bigr)\right\rangle
&=\sum_{a,b=1}^M c_ac_b\left\langle\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\Theta_t[P_a]P_b\bigr)\right\rangle\\
&=\sum_{a,b=1}^M c_ac_bA^t_{ab}.
\end{align}
Hence $c^TA^tc\geq0$ for every $c\in\mathbb{R}^M$, so $A^t\succeq0$. If $F_T^t$ is obtained from a two-dimensional feasible set $F_T$ by adding retained twist-reflection matrices, then the exact assignment remains feasible and $F_T^t\subseteq F_T$. Applying the augmentation theorem gives
\[
L_T\leq L_T^t\leq p\leq U_T^t\leq U_T.
\]
By (P6), this proof supplies no exact $d\geq3$ twist-reflection PSD constraint.

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{d=2:\ A^t\succeq0\text{ is an exact tightening};\qquad d\geq3:\ \text{not certified by this proof}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$

deeper_metadata.revision_intent: Maximize alignment with the JSON schema and with the paper goals by replacing weaker or merely descriptive material with proof-level consequences: certificate soundness, exact augmentation monotonicity, dimension-scoped twist reflection, SU(2) closure, SU(3) affine closure, and path-family closure.

rubric_interpretation.schema: Exactly one JSON object with paper_title, contiguous deeper_reasoning_k strings, and exactly one deeper_metadata object.
rubric_interpretation.latex: Each deeper_reasoning_k is a standalone LaTeX fragment using only article-compatible amsmath and amssymb constructs.
rubric_interpretation.value_standard: Prefer derivations that compose multiple core lemmas into goal-critical consequences, avoid restating individual source proofs, and state scope limitations explicitly.

deeper_reasoning_1.title: Finite certificate soundness
deeper_reasoning_1.goal_alignment: Directly proves the interval-validity predicate required for certified plaquette bounds.
deeper_reasoning_1.scientific_payoff: Connects exact positivity and loop-equation identities to rigorous lower and upper bounds on the plaquette.
deeper_reasoning_1.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Turns separate core constraints into feasible-set containment and infimum/supremum soundness.
deeper_reasoning_1.formal_sharpness: The exact-assignment feasibility assumption is explicit and is traced to retained exact constraints.
deeper_reasoning_1.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids numerical performance claims and avoids merely repeating any single PSD lemma.
controlled_external_lemmas: basic order properties of infimum and supremum
deeper_reasoning_1.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Validity requires the truncation to retain all variables required by its stated constraints; this is encoded in the definition of the feasible set.

deeper_reasoning_2.title: Validity-preserving augmentation monotonicity
deeper_reasoning_2.goal_alignment: Explains why exact added constraints are high value: they preserve validity and weakly reduce width.
deeper_reasoning_2.scientific_payoff: Provides the reusable theorem behind adding twist reflection, more loop equations, or larger closed truncations.
deeper_reasoning_2.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Abstracts the optimization effect of exact constraints rather than restating their derivation.
deeper_reasoning_2.formal_sharpness: Requires both subset inclusion and exact-assignment feasibility.
deeper_reasoning_2.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejects unverified heuristic constraints that may exclude the exact moment assignment.
controlled_external_lemmas: elementary monotonicity of infimum and supremum under set inclusion
deeper_reasoning_2.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The theorem does not claim strict tightening; it correctly states weak tightening.

deeper_reasoning_3.title: Exact two-dimensional twist-reflection tightening
deeper_reasoning_3.goal_alignment: Directly proves the exact d=2 twist-reflection PSD condition and the resulting interval nesting.
deeper_reasoning_3.scientific_payoff: Shows precisely when the additional twist-reflection matrix is a rigorous bootstrap constraint.
deeper_reasoning_3.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Combines the PSD proof with the optimization monotonicity theorem and explicit d>=3 scope control.
deeper_reasoning_3.formal_sharpness: Separates exact d=2 validity from non-certified higher-dimensional use.
deeper_reasoning_3.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids overclaiming approximate higher-dimensional twist reflection as exact.
controlled_external_lemmas: normalization by a positive partition function
deeper_reasoning_3.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The result applies only to path sets meeting the d=2 endpoint and half-plane conditions.

deeper_reasoning_4.title: SU(2) single-trace closure
deeper_reasoning_4.goal_alignment: Covers the N=2 part of the certified-bound goal by proving that independent double traces are unnecessary.
deeper_reasoning_4.scientific_payoff: Explains why the SU(2) bootstrap can be smaller than the SU(3) bootstrap without losing exactness.
deeper_reasoning_4.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Converts the SU(2) loop-equation reduction into a finite variable-closure statement.
deeper_reasoning_4.formal_sharpness: Requires retention of all generated single-trace loops after applying the identity.
deeper_reasoning_4.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids treating SU(2) as a special numerical case only; states the exact algebraic reason for closure.
deeper_reasoning_4.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: The entry does not claim SU(2) bounds are tighter, only that closure needs fewer coordinate types.

deeper_reasoning_5.title: SU(3) single/double-trace affine closure
deeper_reasoning_5.goal_alignment: Directly proves that the SU(3) retained loop equations can be represented without independent triple traces.
deeper_reasoning_5.scientific_payoff: Identifies the exact variable class needed for finite-rank SU(3) beyond the single-trace sector.
deeper_reasoning_5.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Composes single-trace equations, double-trace equations, and triple-trace reduction into one closure result.
deeper_reasoning_5.formal_sharpness: Conditional on retaining every post-reduction single- and double-trace coordinate generated by the selected equations.
deeper_reasoning_5.low_value_rejection_audit: Avoids false large-N factorization; double traces remain independent as required for finite SU(3).
controlled_external_lemmas: substitution of exact algebraic identities into linear constraints
deeper_reasoning_5.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Closure is not automatic for arbitrary truncations; the retention condition is explicitly stated.

deeper_reasoning_6.title: Path-family closure as the criterion for reduced truncations
deeper_reasoning_6.goal_alignment: Connects ladder/plane path selection to certified bounds by requiring closure under generated constraints.
deeper_reasoning_6.scientific_payoff: Prevents reduced path systems from silently becoming heuristic by distinguishing closed retained constraints from missing generated variables.
deeper_reasoning_6.nontrivial_advance_over_sources: Elevates the ladder lemma into a general validity test for dimensional path reduction.
deeper_reasoning_6.formal_sharpness: Proves the ladder case and states the exact closure condition required before applying the same reasoning to plane families.
deeper_reasoning_6.low_value_rejection_audit: Rejects path reduction justified only by computational convenience.
controlled_external_lemmas: set closure under the explicitly retained generation operations
deeper_reasoning_6.known_residual_risks_and_mitigation: Plane-type claims are conditional on verifying the same sewing and insertion closure in the selected subplane.

rejected_low_value_candidates: A standalone restatement of Hermitian positivity, because it is already core_reasoning_1 and does not deepen the goal argument.
A standalone large-N factorization derivation, because the paper goal is finite SU(2)/SU(3) certification and SU(3) double traces must remain independent.
A numerical benchmark or strong-coupling comparison entry, because it is useful context but less central than exact certificate soundness and closure.

global_alignment_audit.top_level_schema: paper_title plus contiguous deeper_reasoning_1 through deeper_reasoning_6 plus exactly one deeper_metadata object; no other top-level keys.
global_alignment_audit.reasoning_value: Every reasoning entry proves a goal-critical consequence rather than copying a source proof verbatim.
global_alignment_audit.core_coverage: Uses positivity, reflection positivity, twist reflection, normalized loop equations, SU(2) reduction, SU(3) single/double-trace equations, triple-trace reduction, and ladder closure.
global_alignment_audit.goal_coverage: Covers certified plaquette intervals, exact d=2 twist-reflection positivity, SU(3) multi-trace closure, and dimensional path-selection methodology.
global_alignment_audit.scope_control: Explicitly avoids claiming exact twist-reflection positivity in d>=3 and avoids replacing finite-SU(3) double traces by large-N factorization.

known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.finite_truncation_closure: Some statements require the chosen truncation to retain all variables generated by its selected constraints; each affected entry states this condition.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.strict_tightening: The monotonicity proof guarantees weak interval tightening, not strict improvement.
known_residual_risks_and_mitigation.plane_family_generalization: The plane-family statement is a closure criterion, not an unconditional proof for every possible plane restriction.
